subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that pauses or aborts active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or keep default steering as boundary-based delivery plus interrupt mode?
rationale: The choice changes shared runtime semantics, channel UX, session-state ownership, and backend compatibility; current main only implements boundary-based steering and partial admission fixes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported default and use related issues only for messages reaching the existing boundary-based policy.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with explicit backend rejection and fallback behavior.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle only after maintainers accept the upgrade and compatibility risk.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest routing candidate from recent active-run steering work and maintainer replacement history on the central runtime paths.
